open_points.subject: initial daily-backup look
open_points.text: `module:instance_lifecycle` runs the look at the interval of the imported `BACKUP_LOOK_SECONDS` constant, 60 seconds
open_points.question: When is the first look made after a successfully started instance begins serving, and what anchors later 60-second looks?
options: Look immediately, then every 60 seconds from that look
Wait 60 seconds before the first look, then repeat
Align looks to UTC wall-clock minute boundaries
open_points.default_guess: Look immediately when serving starts, then use a fixed 60-second cadence.

witness.initial: A full instance begins serving at 02:59:30 UTC and has no kept backup for that date.
events: At 03:00:30 UTC the first post-start 60-second boundary is reached.
outcomes: An immediate first look saw the date before 03:00, so the 03:00:30 look starts the daily backup.
The first look occurs only at 03:00:30, so no earlier look of this process saw that date before 03:00 and no backup starts.
witness.observer: The owner, through the newest-backup display and the files in the backup location.

open_points.subject: backup-look cadence during a long invocation or delayed timer
open_points.question: If an invocation is still running, or the timer cannot execute at a scheduled boundary, are subsequent looks emitted concurrently, skipped, caught up, or delayed until 60 seconds after completion?
options: Keep a fixed-rate cadence and make each look, while `module:backups` refuses to start an overlapping run
Skip boundaries while the invocation is running and resume on the fixed cadence
Use fixed delay, scheduling the next look 60 seconds after the invocation finishes
Catch up missed looks when execution resumes
open_points.default_guess: Use a fixed-rate timer; make the due check at every boundary and let the no-run-going condition prevent overlapping backup runs.

witness.initial: The backup started on day 1 is still running through day 2 at 02:59 UTC and finishes at 02:59:30; day 2 has no kept backup.
events: A scheduled boundary occurs on day 2 before 03:00 while the day-1 run is still going.
The next scheduled boundary is at or after 03:00 after the day-1 run has finished.
outcomes: A fixed-rate implementation performs the pre-03:00 look despite the running backup; the later look satisfies the crossing rule and starts day 2's backup.
A serialized fixed-delay implementation makes no day-2 look before 03:00; its first later look cannot satisfy the crossing rule, so day 2 gets no backup.
witness.observer: The owner, through the newest-backup display and the kept backups.
